Spiraling back

This topic revisits grammar you met earlier, in a harder context: Topic 2, Topic 3, Topic 4, Topic 6, Topic 9.

1

Essential Question

How can I use AI to improve my writing without allowing AI to take responsibility for my work?

2

Teaching & Learning Concepts

The communication principles, workplace expectations, and healthcare context behind this topic.

  • Revising versus proofreading — revising changes what the writing says; proofreading fixes how it is written. Do them in that order.
  • AI as a writing coach: what it is good at, and what it cannot do
  • Prompting for feedback rather than for a rewrite
  • Checking AI suggestions instead of accepting them
  • Hallucination — AI invents facts, citations, and details with complete confidence
  • Privacy and HIPAA: patient information must never be entered into an AI tool
  • You remain responsible for the final content, whatever produced the draft

Human editing versus AI editing

Where each one helps, and where each one fails.

Practice only — nothing here is graded or recorded.

  • 1Which task is AI genuinely good at, in a way you can rely on?
  • 2Which prompt asks AI for coaching rather than for a replacement?
  • 3You want AI feedback on a message you wrote about a specific patient. What must you do first?
  • 4Revising and proofreading — which order, and why?

AI feedback lab

The full chain: your original, the AI's feedback, your evaluation of that feedback, and your revision. Panel 3 is the one that matters.

AI can suggest. You decide.

Never paste patient information into an AI tool — no names, no dates of birth, no identifiable details. Use the practice text below or your own work with every identifier removed.

Need something to work with? Use this draft.

Dear Mr. Osei, Your appointment is coming up soon. Please make sure you don't eat anything beforehand and bring all your stuff. If you have any issues just let us know. We look forward to seeing you. Thanks, The Office

Paste one piece of healthcare writing you produced earlier in this course.

Ask an AI tool for feedback and paste its response here. Ask it to identify unclear wording, grammar problems, and tone — not to rewrite it for you.

Which suggestions are right, and which are wrong or would make it worse? Say why for each. This is the part that is yours.

Rewrite it, using the suggestions you accepted and ignoring the ones you rejected.

0 of 4 panels complete.

Spot the bad AI revision

An AI tool produced the revision below. It reads well. Check every problem you can find before revealing the answers.

Dear Mr. Osei, Your appointment is scheduled for Tuesday, 21 October at 8:30 a.m. Please fast for a minimum of 12 hours beforehand, and bring your insurance card, photo ID, and a complete list of your current medications including dosages. Per CDC guideline 2019-A, patients over 60 should also discontinue anticoagulant therapy 48 hours prior. Warm regards, The Office Team
